newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Poll finds more Swedes than thought favour EMU.
newsitem.headline: Poll finds more Swedes than thought favour EMU.

text.p: A majority of Swedes are in favour of joining the European Union's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), even though they do not want to enter immediately, a new poll published on Wednesday showed.

The poll by SIFO, the Swedish Institute for Public Opinion Research, for the Finans Tidningen newspaper, said that 44 percent of those polled were positive towards Swedish membership while 40 percent were opposed. The remaining 16 percent held no view.
But nearly 60 percent of the supporters, or 26 percent of those polled, want Sweden to put off joining EMU until a later occasion. EMU is due to come into force on January 1, 1999.

An earlier poll of 1,000 Swedes published on November 7 showed that 54 percent would say no to EMU if a referendum on the issue were held at the time of the survey and only 21 percent would vote for joining.
Some 23 percent were uncertain and two percent did not vote in that poll.
